desk.headline: Sales up 1% to $22.7bn, below estimates; adjusted EPS $0.16 missed; no formal guidance
results: Sales edged up 1% to $22.7bn, short of the $23.6bn analysts expected; adjusted EPS fell to $0.16 from $0.54, against $0.32 expected.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped 36% to $1.18bn as chicken (Pilgrim's, -40%), US pork (-83%), Brazil beef (-54%) and Australia (-21%) all weakened.
US beef was the bright spot: margins climbed month by month to 3.9% in September, and EBITDA turned slightly positive on a US GAAP basis.
Free cash flow was -$167m as grain and beef inventories built up, and debt to EBITDA rose to 3.54x from 2.39x.
Liquidity rose to $8.2bn after the credit line was raised to $4.2bn; debt has no large maturities for five years.

guidance.summary: JBS gives no numeric guidance. It said conditions were improving early in Q4 as China buys ahead of its 2027 beef import quota, Brazil heads into its busy season and US beef margins recover.

points: The CEO linked the rise in debt to EBITDA to 3.54x directly to the weaker quarter.
US beef recovered on processing-capacity cuts, the reopening of US-Mexico cattle crossings and strong demand.
Brazil beef exports fell after China's 2026 quota was filled; China demand picked up again at the start of Q4.
US pork suffered from soft demand as inflation squeezed shoppers and from ample global supply.
Seara chicken stayed strongly profitable, with record export volumes in September.
call.source: Company commentary in the press release (Exhibit 99.1) and Investing.com, 9 Nov 2026; no coverage of the 10 Nov call found yet

watch: Whether the US beef margin recovery holds through Q4.
Brazil export volumes as China fills its 2027 quota.
Whether leverage falls back from 3.54x as inventories unwind and cash flow recovers.

sources.title: JBS falls 7% as earnings miss on challenging beef markets — Investing.com, 9 Nov 2026
